title: Honors From National Association of Black Journalists
summary: We are thrilled to share that the National Association of Black Journalists awarded Brent Staples, a longtime Times editorial board member, the Chuck Stone Lifetime Achievement Award.
body_markdown:
Brent Staples won a Lifetime Achievement Award, and The Times received four additional honors. Read more in the below note from Newsroom Culture and Careers’ Ben Schneider.


We are thrilled to share that the National Association of Black Journalists awarded Brent Staples, a longtime Times editorial board member, the Chuck Stone Lifetime Achievement Award.


The Times also won four Salute to Excellence Awards from N.A.B.J.:


- Abdi Latif Dahir, Vivian Nereim and Justin Scheck won in the investigative category, national newspaper, for their[coverage](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/03/16/world/africa/saudi-arabia-kenya-uganda-maids-women.html) of[abuse](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/11/14/world/europe/kenya-president-saudi-arabia-maids.html) and deaths of East African women sent to Saudi Arabia to work in[seemingly safe](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/12/04/world/africa/kenya-diplomat-sex-abuse-women.html) housekeeping jobs.
- Erica Green won for news series by a national newspaper for her coverage of President Trump’s[dismantling](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/02/03/us/politics/trump-diversity-racism.html) of efforts to promote[diversity](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/08/31/us/politics/trump-federal-work-force-black-women.html) in public life and attempts to[sanitize](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/06/20/us/politics/trump-black-history-federal-holidays.html) the country’s history of racism.
- Emmanuel Morgan won for sports coverage by a national newspaper for “[American Sports Are Turning Up the Volume of Afrobeats](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/12/03/arts/music/afrobeats-nba-nfl.html) ,” which explores how musical influence from Nigeria and Ghana is growing in the N.B.A. and in other sports.
- A collaborative investigation between The Times and The Examination, a nonprofit newsroom that reports on global health, won for international reporting, single story news in digital media.Peter S. Goodman and Samuel Granados of The Times and Will Fitzgibbon and the staff of The Examination[investigated](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2025/11/18/world/africa/lead-poisoning-car-battery.html)[how](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/11/18/world/africa/lead-poisoning-auto-industry-car-batteries.html) Nigerian factories that recycle lead in car batteries, which is[sold to U.S. companies](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/11/25/world/africa/lead-battery-recycling-pollution-cars.html) , are poisoning the people working and living nearby.


Brent Staples won the **** Lifetime Achievement Award **** for a storied career, including 35 years as a member of the New York Times editorial board. Brent has won a Pulitzer Prize for editorial writing and written a memoir, “Parallel Time,” which was a finalist for the Los Angeles Times Book Prize and winner of the Anisfield-Wolf Book Award.


The full list of N.A.B.J. winners is[here](https://nabjonline.org/blog/nabj-announces-2026-salute-to-excellence-awards-winners/) and[here](https://nabjonline.org/blog/nabj-announces-2026-hall-of-fame-inductees-special-honors-recipients-2-2/) . Congratulations to all!


— Ben
